title: Exact Frobenius fibres of constructible rational Weil sheaves
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, an integer $a\ge1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ and $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$. Let $Y_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme and put $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$. Let $\Qlb$ be the fixed algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Use constructible $\Qlb$-sheaves in the heart of [def-weil-constructible-heart], with Weil structures and commuting morphisms as in [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. For a closed point $x\in|Y_0|$ choose an embedding $\kappa(x)\hookrightarrow k$ and the associated geometric point $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}k\to Y$. The fibre $\mathcal H_{\bar x}$ means the finite-dimensional rational point fibre and its local geometric Frobenius $F_x$ of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. Then a short exact sequence of such Weil sheaves induces a short exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow\mathcal F'_{\bar x}\longrightarrow\mathcal F_{\bar x}\longrightarrow\mathcal F''_{\bar x}\longrightarrow0$$
of finite-dimensional $\Qlb$-vector spaces, and the two induced maps commute with $F_x$.

source.place: Corollary 6.8.5, Lemma 6.8.7, Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15 (closed-point inverse image); Weil compatibility is the naturality of the local operator

proof.text: Write $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and let $0\to\mathcal F\xrightarrow{i}\mathcal G\xrightarrow{j}\mathcal H\to0$ be the given short exact sequence. Apply [lem-dl-a1-constructible-fibres-exact] at $\bar x:s\to Y$: its statement uses exactly the heart [def-weil-constructible-heart] in the question, computes fibres by derived pullback and the point-fibre functor, and explicitly includes constructible Weil sheaves after forgetting their structure. Its hypotheses hold because $Y_0$ is separated of finite type over $k_0$ and $\ell\ne p$. It gives a short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal F_{\bar x}\xrightarrow{i_{\bar x}}\mathcal G_{\bar x}\xrightarrow{j_{\bar x}}\mathcal H_{\bar x}\to0$ of finite-dimensional $\Qlb$-vector spaces. These are the rational coefficient fibres specified in the question; no assertion about arbitrary pro-etale sheaf stalks is being used.

source.place: Corollary 6.8.5, Lemma 6.8.7, Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15; specialized using the existing constructible coefficient-fibre lemma

proof.text: Apply [lem-wf-common-stage-weil-iterate] to the two given Weil arrows, their structure maps and inverses. For $T=Lg_Y^*$ and $e=[\kappa(x):k_0]\geq1$, it gives the representative-independent common-stage identities $u\theta_K^{[e]}=\theta_L^{[e]}T^e(u)$. Apply [lem-wf-common-stage-point-return] to the $\mathbf F_{q^e}$-point specified by the chosen residue embedding. For $P=\operatorname{Fib}_sL\bar x^*$ it gives $P(T^eu)J_K=J_LP(u)$, including the normalized scalar-extension, identity and tower comparisons. Both results apply to arbitrary Weil morphisms; neither arrow needs to be an isomorphism.

source.place: Opening punctual-bounds argument; expansion of the local Frobenius definition and the equation for a Weil morphism

proof.text:
The definition [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] gives $F_{x,K}=P(\theta_K^{[e]})J_K$ at every finite coefficient stage. The two preceding lemmas identify these factors after every further common extension, so this formula defines the same operator in the common-stage point category. For either arrow $u:K\to L$, functoriality and Step 2 give
$$P(u)F_{x,K}=P(u\theta_K^{[e]})J_K=P(\theta_L^{[e]})P(T^eu)J_K=P(\theta_L^{[e]})J_LP(u)=F_{x,L}P(u).$$
Apply $H^0$ to this equality. By the fibre convention in the same definition these are exactly the rational fibre maps and the local geometric Frobenius operators in Step 1, proving both equivariance assertions.
